    An Aronszajn tree of bounded increasing rational sequences (Construction 4.3) #

    Following Jech [Je, proof of Theorem 9.16], we construct by recursion on α < ω₁ countable sets T_α of strictly increasing bounded sequences of rationals of length α. A node of level α is modelled as a function ω₁ → ℚ vanishing from α on.

    • T_α = {∅} for the least α;
    • T_{γ+1} consists of the extensions of nodes f ∈ T_γ by one value p > f;
    • for a limit α, T_α consists of the limits of chains through a cofinal sequence of levels, starting at a node f ∈ T_β below a and staying below rationals increasing to b > a.

    By induction, every level is countable, closed under restriction, and has the extension property (9.10): every node of level β ≤ α bounded by a < q extends to a node of level α bounded by some a' < q. A compatible family would give a strictly increasing map ω₁ → ℚ, which is impossible, so the inverse limit of the levels is empty.

                            structure ExtriangulatedRealization.Aronszajn.Good (α : Omega1) :
                            Prop

                            The invariants of the level α: nodes vanish from α on, are strictly increasing and bounded below α; the levels are closed under restriction, have the extension property (9.10), and are countable.

                            • restr_self (f : Omega1 → ℚ) : f ∈ tree α → restr α f = f
                            • strictMono (f : Omega1 → ℚ) : f ∈ tree α → ∀ (ξ η : Omega1), ξ < η → η < α → f ξ < f η
                            • bdd (f : Omega1 → ℚ) : f ∈ tree α → ∃ (q : ℚ), Below α f q
                            • closed (f : Omega1 → ℚ) : f ∈ tree α → ∀ β ≤ α, restr β f ∈ tree β
                            • ext (β : Omega1) : β ≤ α → ∀ f ∈ tree β, ∀ (a q : ℚ), Below β f a → a < q → ∃ g ∈ tree α, restr β g = f ∧ ∃ a' < q, Below α g a'
